Bug.Description: Recursive fault on system check (critical or lower) due to poor DIAG X'288' hercules patch
Bug.Behavior: If any subsystem of the kernel triggers a system check (critical or lower), kernel will recursively fault with Operation Exception, and/or trigger a restart (due to misconfigured timebomb)
Bug.Solution: Patches Hercules DIAG X'288' Patch to be more robust (also mirror linux)

Bug.Description: IRQ descriptor table slot-number allocation mismatch causes all SCOMS-managed IRQ dispatch to silently fail, posting no handlers for any external interrupt (clock comparator, CPU timer, IPI, etc.)
Bug.Behavior:
register() called g_irq_table.alloc() which pulled an arbitrary free-list slot index S, populating m_slots[S] with the handler. irq_dispatch() and find_raw() look up slots by the IRQ vector number V (so m_slots[V]), which remained with ko.id == KOBJECT_ID_INVALID. The lookup returned nullptr and the handler was never invoked.
Consequence: ext.cxxm routed every external interrupt through the IRQ table (instead of direct fast paths), so clock comparator events, CPU timer ticks, timing alerts, service signals, and IPI vectors all produced zero dispatch work. Without timer-driven scheduler ticks the BSP stopped advancing, and APs entering sched_init_ap simultaneously raced raw PMM allocations with no scheduler heartbeat, yielding nondeterministic PMM free-list corruption (assert_allocatable_frame with frame_owner::stack, order 2), deadlocks (254/255 progress stall), or undefined spin-wait hangs.
Bug.Solution:
Introduced scoms_table::alloc_at(u32 id) which claims a specific slot index by unlinking it from the SCOMS free-list rather than taking an arbitrary slot from the free-list head. irqdesc::register() now calls alloc_at(irq) so the irq_desc for vector V always occupies m_slots[V], making find_raw(V) reach the correct descriptor.
Additional benefit: alloc_at() is robust against reuse of a slot by a different IRQ vector — if m_slots[id].ko.id != KOBJECT_ID_INVALID, the call returns already_locked, which replaces the silent double-registration that existed before.

Bug.Description: __schedule early-return path leaves the re-picked strand with substate==runnable instead of substate==running.
Bug.Behavior:
In sched::schedule() the prev strand is enqueued (or kept runnable) at L423-L437 — its substate is set to sched_substate::runnable. When select_next() then picks the same strand again (next == prev), the function takes the early-return branch (L477-L481) and skips the next->substate = sched_substate::running transition at L494.
Consequence: any strand that yields and is immediately re-picked retains substate==runnable even though it IS the running strand. This was exposed by dom_op::strand_query_state (user/init/init.S Test 57) which read the primary strand's substate from inside a running SVC handler and observed substate==1 (runnable) instead of substate==2 (running). Beyond the test failure, the bug silently corrupts any scheduler introspection or migration logic that consults strand.substate on the running strand to decide whether the CPU is currently committed.
Bug.Solution: Set next->substate = sched_substate::running before the early-return from the next==prev branch in __schedule. This is the same transition the long-form handoff path performs at L494; the early-return was simply missing it.

Bug.Description: cap::acquire syscall retained the removed forgeable type/id ABI instead of accepting a nucleus-issued source capability token
Bug.Behavior: user/init passed cap_type, domain id, and requested rights to cap::acquire. The nucleus interpreted the first argument as an opaque token, so the reconstructed value failed capability-slot generation and ownership validation.
Bug.Solution: Bootstrap now supplies an all-rights nucleus-issued source token through the preserved init ABI register. cap::acquire derives only from that token, while the init tests use the opaque token for admin, map, and delegate derivation.

Bug.Description: Domain names retained temporary user-buffer pointers and secondary strands retained SCOMS parent dependencies during teardown
Bug.Behavior: The domain-create syscall passed a stack-local copied name to domain_create(), leaving dgp::domain::name dangling. Later teardown logs printed empty or corrupted names. Domain destruction also released secondary strand slots without detaching them from the domain, so the final domain release could fail with live dependents.
Bug.Solution: Domains now own a bounded inline name buffer and copy names into it during creation. Secondary strand teardown detaches each strand from its domain before releasing its SCOMS slot.

Bug.Description: Domain teardown discarded the VM address-space pointer before releasing its SCOMS object
Bug.Behavior: vm_destroy_space() cleared vm_space.address_space_object after removing regions. domain_destroy() therefore skipped the address-space object release, leaving the domain object with a live SCOMS dependent and causing dom::destroy to return generic::invalid_arg.
Bug.Solution: VM teardown now leaves the address-space object reference for domain_destroy() to release after all region and memory-object children have been detached. Domain teardown also drains IPC endpoints, policy registrations, and named services owned by the dying domain.

Bug.Description: vm_region alloc_region double-constructed the slot, wiping the SCOMS id assigned by scoms_table::alloc
Bug.Behavior: alloc_region() called ::new((void*)rgn) vm_region{} after g_region_table.alloc() had already default-constructed the slot and initialised ko.id via ko.initialize(slot, type). The placement-new zero-initialised the storage, clearing ko.id back to ~0U. Capabilities issued against such a region therefore failed lookup_kobject() (cap_issue returned generic::not_found) and every operation that relied on a valid region ko.id — shm_export, lazy revocation, region teardown — was broken.
Bug.Solution: Removed the redundant placement-new and the ko.type reassignment. alloc_region now only fills in the user-visible fields (va_start, va_end, prot, flags, backing, phys_base) and activates the embryo ref. ko.id and ko.type are preserved from scoms_table::alloc().

Bug.Description: gate_find() conflates the packed nucleus-call number with a gate id
Bug.Behavior: dgp/gate dispatch (dispatch.cxx:226) looks up gates by the packed nr instead of a pure gate id; wrong-slot resolution corrupts dispatch and can mask as gate_count corruption.
Bug.Solution: R0: split gate-id domain from packed call numbers; R2: gate table replaced entirely by PC-ss ETE/LTE machinery.
Bug.Notes: R0 fix 2026-10-09: gate validation runs only for ops carrying a real meta.gate_id; the packed call number is never a gate slot id. R2 replaces the table with ETE/LTE machinery.

Bug.Description: PMM free() marks the freed block as buddy-owned before linking it

Bug.Description: Tick-timer double-insert at hotplug re-online (stale per-CPU timer heap + forced armed flag)
Bug.Behavior: A stopped CPU cannot cancel its own timers (timer_cancel must run on the timer CPU), so the per-CPU timer heap survives offline with stale armed entries. scheduler_cpu_attach then forced t.armed=false and re-added the AP tick timer into a heap still holding it - defeating timer_add's armed guard (timer core.cxx:87) - producing a double entry, double fire and heap corruption on any offline/online cycle. Root enabler: timer::init_ap was a declared no-op that never reset the heap.
Bug.Solution: Fixed 2026-10-10: timer::init_ap now resets the CPU heap and disarms every dropped timer; the armed-flag force in scheduler_cpu_attach is removed so timer_add's guard stands. Hotplug cycle test owed at R4 (RC-10.4, OBL-009).
Bug.Notes: Found while auditing the BUG-037 fix; never previously filed. Tracked: OBL-014 in docs/architecture/REALIZATION.md.

Bug.Description: EEVDF_DEFAULT_SLICE_NS held a TOD-tick value (40'960'000) in an _NS-named constant — every fair slice was 40.96 ms, not the §9.2-mandated 2.5 ms
Bug.Behavior: fair.zcomponent/core.cxxm:27 defined the slice as "TOD ticks" (the 10 ms tick interval in TOD units) while every consumer (sched_slice, place_entity, cpu_timer_tick deadline math, cputimer_arm_ns) treated it as nanoseconds. Once CR0.53 enabled real SPT delivery, schedule() faithfully armed 40.96/n ms quanta — rotation slots became LONGER than the pre-CPU-timer 10 ms tick rotation, regressing the suite from ~8 s to ~18 s (T76 measured 41.2 ms/yield = exactly 3 slots of 40.96/3 ms; T78 identical per-try cost). Root cause of the 2026-10-24 16:34 capture.
Bug.Solution: Constant corrected to 2'500'000 ns per ch. 9.2 (2026-10-24). Verification pending owner capture.
Bug.Notes: Found by quantitative slot analysis of the owner's GCC capture; the constant's own comment said "in TOD ticks".

Bug.Description: cpu_timer_tick re-armed SPT with raw nanoseconds and never recorded the armed TOD value
Bug.Behavior: sched/core.cxx:756 called cputimer::spt(curr->se.slice) with se.slice in ns while SPT takes TOD units (4096/us), and g_cputimer_armed_tod was not updated — the next tick charged against the stale arm (4x overcharge per premature fire; a 2.5 ms slice fired every ~610 us). Residual of the same unit-boundary class as the vruntime fix; violated the §9.2 One Time Base law at the re-arm site.
Bug.Solution: Re-arm through detail::cputimer_arm_ns (converts and records) (2026-10-24). Verification pending owner capture.

Bug.Description: fair::tick charged a fixed slice of vruntime on every 10 ms periodic tick — double accounting once the CPU timer went live
Bug.Behavior: fair.zcomponent/core.cxx fair::tick called update_curr with a fixed EEVDF_DEFAULT_SLICE_NS delta every periodic tick. This was the legacy stopgap from the era when SPT expiry was never delivered; with cpu_timer_tick charging measured elapsed, every quantum was billed twice (and in fixed, not measured, units), violating ch. 9.3 (SPT drives the fair quantum; the periodic tick drives accounting and balancing).
Bug.Solution: fair::tick reduced to a deadline-expiry safety re-check (extend + need_resched), no charging (2026-10-24). Verification pending owner capture.

Bug.Description: Far-future clock-comparator arm used 40'960'000 TOD (10 ms) where 10 seconds was intended
Bug.Behavior: timer.zcomponent/core.cxx rearm_comparator and irq_handler_timing_alert armed the comparator at stck()+40'960'000 with the comment "~10 seconds"; the value is 10 ms in TOD units, so idle CPUs with empty timer heaps woke at 100 Hz. Same TOD/ns confusion family as BUG-052.
Bug.Solution: Both sites corrected to 40'960'000'000 TOD (2026-10-24). Verification pending owner capture.

Bug.Description: avg_vruntime accumulator leaked w × Δmin_vruntime per queue transit — newly placed strands starved for ~boot_time/queue_depth
Bug.Behavior: fair.zcomponent avg_vruntime_add recorded w × (vruntime − min_vruntime@enqueue) while avg_vruntime_sub removed w × (vruntime − min_vruntime@dequeue); min_vruntime advances between the two snapshots (the running strand drags it), so every enqueue/dequeue transit left a permanent residual. Σ residuals ≈ weight × total queued-time = w × boot_time × queue_depth, drifting the computed average ahead of min_vruntime by ≈ T/n_queued. place_entity takes base = max(avg, min_vruntime), so every newly created strand was placed that far into the future. Measured (2026-10-24 capture, post-BUG-052 fix): T79 worker created at t=4.287 s did not run until t=5.765 s — 1.478 s ≈ T/3 with weight-sum 3×1024, exactly the predicted drift; T78's ~0.85 s worker-start matches T/4. join wake (17 µs) and sleep (22.1 ms for 20 ms) were healthy — the entire residual cost of tests 78/79 was this drift.
Bug.Solution: Absolute weighted sum: accumulator holds Σ w_i × vruntime_i; add/sub cancel exactly because vruntime only changes while a strand is off the tree (2026-10-24). Verification pending owner capture.
Bug.Notes: Diagnosed from the T79PROBE lines (exit wake_us=17, join iters=1 total_us=1478622, sleep total_us=22141). Confirmed by the 2026-10-24 close-out captures: GCC join 5 us (iters=0), LLVM 15.6 ms, T78/T79 milliseconds, 78/78 both toolchains.

Bug.Description: Fair rotation cadence sits above the armed slice — 3x on GCC, 9x+ on LLVM; scheduler-latency paths inflate on the LLVM build
Bug.Behavior: Post-BUG-052..056 captures (2026-10-24, both toolchains, 78/78 PASS): GCC T76 = 7.5 ms/yield (model: ~2.5-5 ms), sleep exact (21.7 ms/20 ms), join 5 us. LLVM T76 = 67.5 ms/yield, sleep(20 ms) total 70 ms (= 7 ticks), join worker-start 15.5 ms (~6 slots). The inflation is non-uniform (boot-to-T75 only ~40% slower on LLVM) so host contention alone does not explain it; all scheduler-latency paths inflate together while correctness is unaffected (no lost wake, no starvation). Hypothesis: per-fire charge undercount on the LLVM build (deadline taking multiple SPT fires to expire) or wake-to-resume latency in the fair pick; needs one probe round with a per-fire charge histogram and pick-cadence counters on the LLVM nucleus.
Bug.Solution: Probe round on the LLVM build: charge histogram in cpu_timer_tick (fires, elapsed_ns, armed) + schedule() pick cadence; fix whatever it exposes. Not a correctness blocker; R2 continues in parallel.
Bug.Notes: Filed at the close of the 2026-10-24 performance arc (BUG-052..056 confirmed by the same captures). CLOSED same day: the calm-host LLVM capture passed 79/79 in 3.39 s with T76 = 834 ms (vs 6.75 s under load) and B057 probes showing elapsed == armed on every fire — fair cadence was host-side interrupt delivery latency under a loaded host, not a kernel defect. Charges exact on both toolchains.

Bug.Description: Suspected cross-CPU fair-tree race (steal vs enqueue) corrupting user .bss with rb-tree link stores during strand creation
Bug.Behavior: CLOBBERPROBE forensics (GCC, 2026-10-24 17:45/17:51 boots): after t41's strand_create the .bss cluster is intact (child=3 dom=2 cap=valid); after t42's strand_create it is wiped — child_id/domain_id/admin_cap/gate_id zeroed and io_token overwritten with a pointer-shaped value, a ~72-byte mostly-zero+pointer pattern over [domain_id..io_token] exactly matching rb_link_node/rb_erase parent/null-child stores through a stale node pointer. Context: t41's worker (strand 256) is stolen to another CPU inside the same window (B057 lines from cp244/cp127 fire between the probes) while t42's create enqueues strand 257 into cpu0's fair tree — the two sides race on the shared tree. LLVM boots have not hit it; the window's width is compiler-scheduling-dependent, so the toolchain split is a hit-rate difference, not immunity. Test 46 (dom::destroy of child_id==0) is the visible casualty; domain_id/admin_cap zeroing means any later syscall would fail too.
Bug.Solution: Bisect boot shipped with try_steal_strand_locked disabled: if t42-mid reads clean, the race is localized to the steal path's cross-CPU dequeue/migrate under the double rq lock; fix by re-auditing the lock/unlock and rb ownership discipline between enqueue_strand (cpu0) and try_steal (remote CPU), including the unlocked topology/snapshot reads. Verification: clean t42-mid with steal re-enabled after the fix.
Bug.Notes: ROOT CAUSE (2026-10-24, kernel exonerated): the user-init worker trampolines set r15 = stack+4080 with no s390x ABI callee register-save headroom; the worker C prologue's stmg %r6,%r15,48(%r15) spills 80 bytes at r15+48..+120 — 96 bytes past the 4096-byte stack array into adjacent .bss. Register-for-register match with the corruption (r6/r8/r10 zeros landing on domain_id/admin_cap/child_id; saved r15 = 0x40E1B0 stamped into io_token). Latent in all pre-existing worker trampolines (t73/t74/t78/t79) — their spills landed in harmless neighbors until the t41/t42 stacks were placed next to the identity cluster. The GCC-vs-LLVM split was .bss layout luck. FIX: all six trampolines reserve the 160-byte ABI frame (aghi 4080 → 3920). The kernel-side B058 canary watch caught the event at exit-in; migration was exonerated by the zero-migration boot (earlier cp-attributed B057 lines were a global-counter print artifact).

Bug.Description: shm import ABI dropped the portal id — imported portals were unreleasable from user space; every import leaked a portal (pinned frames, held AR, ASTE slot) toward the 16-per-domain cap
Bug.Behavior: nc_shm_import returned only ar_num although portal_binding carries portal_id; no shm_unimport exists and nb_portal_destroy needs the id — user space could never destroy an imported binding. t66/t67 portals survived t69 "cleanup" on every boot, holding ar1/ar2 and pinning freed frames; later tests then bound onto leaked state (the T80 maze: fresh imports landed on occupied ranges/ARs, making failures nondeterministic in shape).
Bug.Solution: ABI fixed 2026-10-24: import returns (portal_id << 32) | ar_num (t66/t67 asserts updated); t69 now performs full teardown surface — portals destroyed before token release and page free. R2 ABI window per ch. 18. Verification pending capture.
Bug.Notes: Found while diagnosing T80's retry-leg failure; the suite carried the leak since t66 landed.

Bug.Description: Dispatch target resolution read portal_destroy's a1 as a domain id — destroys of portals with id != 0 authorized against unrelated domains
Bug.Behavior: target_domain_for_op lumped portal_destroy with ops whose a1 is a target domain id. Portal destroy's a1 is the PORTAL id: id 0 collided with the nucleus (authorize passed by accident — every historical destroy), and id 1 resolved to a dead child-domain slot and was denied (t69's second sequential destroy). Owner teardown of multiple portals was architecturally impossible.
Bug.Solution: portal_destroy resolves the acted-upon domain through the portal's source_domain (2026-10-24). Third arg-semantic mismatch this arc (a3 entry-va, import return packing, a1 dual meaning) — pattern class: per-op argument schemas are implicit in scattered switch arms; a declared arg-schema table is the unification. Pending capture.

Bug.Description: percpu field inserted mid-struct shifted the qspinlock MCS node array — cross-CPU lock writes at stale offsets corrupted kernel stacks (found by the stress framework's first stolen-strand run)
Bug.Behavior: pending_dead_strand (reaper handoff, OBL-020) was inserted before ec_bits "as an appended tail" — a false claim: every later field shifted 8 bytes, including qnodes[], whose cross-CPU addressing is percpu-base-relative. Single-CPU boots (the whole t1-t80 era) never exercised cross-CPU node writes; the stress framework's first cross-CPU stolen strand triggered remote qnode writes at stale offsets; cp161 died with ssp_check_fail in cpu_timer_tick (corrupted stack canary). dom_exec of the correctly disk-loaded bench ELF preceded it — the entire driver/VTOC/exec pipeline was verified working in the same capture.
Bug.Solution: Field moved to the absolute tail of percpu_data with a layout law comment (2026-10-25). Rule recorded: percpu_data is an ABI struct — new fields go to the tail only, never mid-struct. Pending capture.
Bug.Notes: The stress framework's first multi-domain IPL found a latent SMP-corruption bug the 80-test suite could never reach.

Bug.Description: uaccess mvcos_copy never decremented the remaining length — every copy over 4 KiB walked both pointers through memory forever, overwriting all storage past the destination
Bug.Behavior: uaccess.cxxm mvcos_copy: on CC=3 (PoP 10-73: effective length = min(true,4096); more remains) the loop advanced pointers by 4096 but assigned `len = chunk` — chunk being the unchanged length — so the loop never terminated: each iteration re-issued MVCOS with the full true length at advanced addresses, copying 4 KiB strides through arbitrary memory. First-ever >4 KiB kernel copy (dom_exec's 20 KiB image copy) triggered it; cpu0 never returned from copy_from_user, and the walking writer trampled shared kernel structures — the AP operation-exception storms, stack-canary fatals, and recursive faults of the whole stress bring-up were this single loop. All prior kernel copies (names, IPC payloads, futex words) were <=4 KiB, which returns CC=0 on the first iteration.
Bug.Solution: `len = chunk - MVCOS_MAX_CHUNK` per PoP 10-72 loop discipline (2026-10-25). Pending capture.
Bug.Notes: Found via PoP cross-check demanded by the owner after the chunked-copy probe pinned the monolithic 20 KiB copy; latent since the uaccess module landed.

Bug.Description: Domain exit wedges the machine — after a non-primary domain's dom_exit, the scheduler never runs another strand (reproduced twice; orchestrator frozen post-selftest-exit)
Bug.Behavior: The selftest domain (exec'd via dom_exec, child-owned cap) ran user code, printed, failed its DASD bind, and called nb_dom_exit — after which the whole system stopped scheduling: the orchestrator strand never resumed (no further console output, 158-line logs ending at the child's exit). The cap path is exonerated (child acquire SUCCEEDED after the owner fix); the wedge is in the exit/teardown path — dom_exit parking the caller's primary, teardown quiesce/reap, or the finish-task-switch handoff interacting with domain destruction. Isolated by retiring the exiting discriminator (bench domains park, never exit) so the stress chain proceeds; the teardown defect remains open for a dedicated fix round.
Bug.Solution: Open: dedicated round on strand/domain exit teardown (park primary, quiesce, destroy, reap) under the stress framework once the storm runs green; the bench fleet parks instead of exiting so the framework is not blocked on it.
Bug.Notes: Second capture-confirmed milestone in the same boot: child-owned delegation cap validated (selftest acquire succeeded); bench fleet widened to 3 domains.

Bug.Description: MVCOS fixup path retries a faulting copy forever — 33k identical region-first translation exceptions on one bad user pointer, no abort
Bug.Behavior: A copy_from_user with a bad source pointer (svc_lookup handler arg mismatch — the caller passed a capability token where the name pointer belonged) faulted mid-MVCOS; the exception-table fixup consumer redirected and RE-EXECUTED the same faulting copy 33,096 times at the same VA (0x8000000001000201, the token as address) — the kernel never aborted the copy nor killed the domain. This is the EX_TYPE_UA_MVCOS_FROM consumer — the exact path OBL-005 flagged as never audited. The mvcos_copy loop's CC handling cannot make progress on a fixup bounce; the copy must abort with a residual/partial indicator instead.
Bug.Solution: Open: audit EX_TYPE_UA_MVCOS_FROM/TO fixup consumers (OBL-005) — a faulting page must terminate the loop with the partial count, not bounce. Triggered by a user-side arg bug (svc_lookup takes a0=name; fixed in the orchestrator); the kernel-side non-abort remains regardless of caller correctness.

Bug.Description: Reuse-form PC number packed LSI at EA bit 44 (form selector) and set_lftd hand-shifted the LFTD origin into the wrong bit window — cross-domain PCs faulted as 32-bit-form garbage walks
Bug.Behavior: Two packing defects in the ASN-LX-reuse landing exposed by the first cross-domain PC storm: (a) gate_materialize wrote lsi at field bit 0 of the lx record — EA bit 44, the 20/32-bit form selector — so every PC took the 32-bit form and translated garbage (stack-full storms at the pcnum-as-address); (b) set_lftd packed (phys>>8)<<8 by hand, misplacing the 23-bit origin inside the designation word → PC-translation-spec/special-op 0x0013 even with correct numbers. The kernel's containment held throughout: faults classified, nullified, domain terminated by signal default, nucleus alive.
Bug.Solution: Mint per PoP 5-35 (lx = lfi | lsi<<7; walk decode lfi=lx&0x7F, lsi=(lx>>7)&0x1F); set_lftd rewritten through the lib.bitfield DSL record (hand bit-shifts banned — standing rule); LFTD word verified numerically (2026-10-25). Pending capture.
Bug.Notes: 2026-10-25 addendum: the LFTD fix alone was insufficient — the capture still faulted (stack-full at pcnum 0x8000, then special-op). Root cause #3, the decisive one: the pc_number RECORD layout itself (lx@12-23, ex@24-31) never matched the canonical operand layout. Hyperion's esa390.h PC_* masks (the authoritative reference implementation layout, cross-checked against its program_call walk in control.c:2996-3230): EX bits 0-7, LX/LSX bits 8-12(19), LFX2 bits 13-18, form selector bit 19, LFX1 bits 20-31 (canonicalized with >>1). Mint, walk, and revoke all recomposed on those masks; classic layout (lx<<8|ex) matches zLinux PC-number convention. Every decode site now reads the raw word.

Bug.Description: Linkage-stack header/trailer entries violated the PoP 5-12 LSHE/LSTE word layout — word 0 must be reserved, word 1 carries the section link, words 2-3 the descriptor
Bug.Behavior: Our header_entry placed the backward link in words 0-1 (PoP reserves word 0 for the control program; the link lives in word 1) and the trailer had NO forward-address word — only an entry descriptor. Hercules' form_stack_entry FETCH_DW's word 1 of the trailer for the forward section header address, i.e. it read our descriptor bytes (entry type / section id) as the address — producing garbage forward addresses (the 0x3ffffff400-class TEIDs) and stack-full exception storms on every PC that needed the trailer/growth path. Self-domain gates (t70-73) never exhausted the initial section's free space, so the trailer was never consulted — first cross-domain storm walked straight into it.
Bug.Solution: header_entry/trailer_entry rewritten to PoP word layout: reserved(4) + section_link V+address(4) + entry_descriptor(8); single-section forward link V=0 (last-section state); stack_init/stack_grow/forensics aligned; layouts composed through lib.bitfield named records (2026-10-25). Pending capture.

Bug.Description: Bootstrap-launched init domain never had its linkage stack seeded — CR15 was 0 (architecturally empty stack) on the primary strand for the entire life of the kernel
Bug.Behavior: stack_init is called only by dom_exec; bootstrap set uregs + entered user mode directly with body->linkage_stack unseeded, so init's CR15 was 0 since boot. The cr15=0 stack-full capture proved it: the orchestrator's first cross-domain PC had no section to grow from, and the nullify/grow path built state on a zero base. t70-73 self-domain PCs "worked" only because small-LX walks never touched the unseeded machinery. Every domain primary launched by bootstrap was PC-incapable since R1.5.
Bug.Solution: strandctx::seed_primary_linkage_stack exported and called by bootstrap before first user entry (2026-10-25); dom_exec children were already seeded. Pending capture.

Bug.Description: CR15 loaded only inside the ASCE-change branch of schedule() — per-strand linkage state went stale/zero across same-space dispatches
Bug.Behavior: The linkage stack address is per-STRAND state (PoP 5-12), but schedule() only wrote CR15 inside the branch guarded by next_owner/asce-differs; the per-strand SAVE ran unconditionally after every switch. A same-ASCE round trip (caller → stolen worker → caller) returned the caller to user mode with CR15 still holding the last strand's value — or 0 on a first switch. Explains cr15=0 persisting after the BUG-067 seed (the seed ran, but a same-space switch zeroed it before the storm) and boot-to-boot variance.
Bug.Solution: Unconditional per-strand CR15 load in the next_owner leg of schedule() (skipping unseeded strands), duplicate inner write removed (2026-10-25). Pending capture.

Bug.Description: Borrowed-space pgm path consumed a linkage stack entry on ANY fault — a plain fault during a PC unstacked the caller's state and restored a garbage PSW (specification exception at a user VA with a kernel PSW)
Bug.Behavior: The borrowed-space check (cr1 != attached) ran state_entry_restore+unstack for every program check regardless of class. A fault inside a live PC region (e.g. a caller faulting while a callee's state entry sits stacked) unstacked the CALLEE's entry and restored ITS PSW into the caller's frame — the follow-on capture showed a specification exception at init's 0x4007c0 executed with PSW 0x07C5 (supervisory DAT-on) at a user address: an unstacked kernel PSW stuffed into a user frame. PoP 5-12: only PR/stack-operation exceptions (and PC-related translation classes) consume stacked state.
Bug.Solution: Borrowed-space unstack restricted to stacked-state exception classes (PGM_STACK_OPERATION 0x0034, PGM_STACK_SPECIFICATION 0x0033, PC-translation-spec, PC/PR translation family) (2026-10-25). Pending capture.

Bug.Description: nc_ipc_endpoint_create reads a0 as peer domain id — no capability parameter at all, contradicting every cap-addressed sibling and the nuclbase wrapper's (cap, peer) shape
Bug.Behavior: The handler takes a0 = peer and derives the caller from current_domain; the nuclbase wrapper and bench passed (admin_cap, peer) — the cap's low bits became the peer id and endpoint_create failed at domain_find/authorize ("no endpoint" x3 in the storm capture). The old t64 suite passed because it called the raw op with the peer in a0 directly. Same per-op argument-schema class as BUG-060: the svc layer's implicit per-op arg meanings diverge between wrapper and handler.
Bug.Solution: Bench fixed to pass peer in a0 (2026-10-25). The schema table (BUG-060 note) remains the unification: declare per-op argument roles once for wrapper, dispatcher, and handler.

Bug.Description: Steal-balancer scoring made cross-NUMA migration arithmetically unreachable — 48-point distance penalty vs ~1.1×load contribution required load≈74 runnable strands on one CPU before any steal
Bug.Behavior: steal_source_score: load contributes load*(capacity+1024)/1024 ≈ 1.1×load while relation distance costs 16/level; same_numa_node (the tier EVERY same-drawer cpu pair falls into) costs 48 against BALANCE_MIN_SCORE=32. With the storm's 2-3 runnable strands on cpu0 the score was ≈ −45: 255 idle APs each correctly ran their pull balance every tick and correctly refused to steal — all guest work serialized on cpu0 for the entire suite (3.79ms/trip × 1500 = the 5.7s "stall", zero work off cpu0 in every capture).
Bug.Solution: BALANCE_MIN_SCORE 32→8; distance penalty 16/level→8/level; load term ×8-scaled BEFORE the division — integer truncation at 1.1×load (2*1124/1024 == 2 in int math) was eating the entire fractional gain, so intermediate tunings still died below load 10. Final: same-NUMA steals at load 4+, SMT-tier at load 2 (2026-10-25). Pending capture: bench strands should spread across APs.

Bug.Description: Cross-CPU PC-ss corruption unlocked by BUG-071 spread: supervisor-mode PSW at a user VA after first real steals — nondeterministic fault-or-stall
Bug.Behavior: After the balancer fix made steals actually fire, the storm became a lottery: either an operation exception with SUPERVISOR PSW (mask 0x07A5..., DAT-on) executing at a USER VA inside the bench image (R0=0x5A5A — callee code ran), with garbage at the faulting instruction, or a silent stall. Never occurred while all work was serialized on cpu0 (every prior capture). The linkage-stack/CR15 discipline was never audited for strands migrating across CPUs mid-PC; the supervisor-bit corruption indicates a state-entry or restore path writing a kernel PSW mask into a user frame — a race or stale-CR15 class defect that serialized execution masked entirely.
Bug.Solution: Open. PCPROBE instrumentation shipped (dispatch-time unseeded-strand dump with stale CR15 readback; pgm supervisor-PSW-at-user-VA dump with strand + CR15). One capture names the mechanism; the fix then targets the named organ. The §5.12 cross-CPU linkage-stack audit is the owed consolidation for this whole defect family (BUG-065..072).
Bug.Notes: The family pattern: each fix unmasked the next latent defect that serialized execution had hidden. The audit — not another spot fix — is what closes it.
